categories.definition: Reference-only galleries of live websites, product/app screens, user flows, navigation patterns and recorded micro-interactions. You study them for patterns and craft; nothing is installed or exported.

Non-web visual references (branding case studies, print flyers, book covers, patterns and textures) plus the moodboard app used to collect them. This is where a direction escapes web-template sameness.

Resources that put design decisions into words, tokens or checklists: named-aesthetic indexes, style guides for prompting, DESIGN.md token files for coding agents, and UX completeness checklists and audit skills.
React/Tailwind components, animated components, page sections and templates you copy or install as source (shadcn registries, CLIs, MCP servers) into your own repo.
Runtime packages and snippets for animation: tweening/timeline engines, smooth scroll, physics micro-interactions and loaders. These are motion primitives, not full UI components.

Browser tools that generate backgrounds, gradients, patterns, particle or shader effects, or apply treatments (dither, halftone, ASCII, contours) to images and video. Output is files or small code exports, not a hosted project.
Tools for choosing or generating color palettes and scales, and for creating custom fonts.
Libraries of ready-made illustration or imagery that can go on a site, subject to each item's license.

Hosted editors with their own canvas, file format or hosting: HTML/CSS design canvases, interactive and Lottie animation authoring, no-code site builders and brand asset hubs. Usually seat-priced SaaS.
Prompt- and credit-driven AI products that generate UI directions, full sites, interactive visual effects, or images and video.

tiers.Core: Reach for it constantly when building a portfolio.
tiers.Strong: Very useful for most portfolio builds.
tiers.Situational: Useful for specific needs or styles.
tiers.Low fit: Off-target for portfolio sites (wrong platform, dated, or unrelated).
